reports.title: Nordic Statistics database
reports.description: Joint statistical database maintained by the Nordic Council of Ministers, drawing on the five Nordic NSIs, the Nomesco-Nososco health/welfare committees and international sources including Eurostat and the OECD.
reports.cadence_note: Roughly monthly, skipping January and July — confirmed via the publisher's own news archive showing distinct dated update posts in the other 10 months across 2023-2025.

release_schedule.note: The Nordic Statistics database is not a discrete annual report but a continuously maintained database. The publisher's news archive (nordicstatistics.org/news) shows a consistent multi-year pattern of roughly monthly 'X update' releases in Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov and Dec of each year from 2022-2025, with no updates posted in January or July. The 'About' page states only that 'Data is updated regularly over the year' without a fixed calendar. Exact day-of-month varies (e.g. August updates landed on 2024-08-22 and 2025-08-29), so entries use month precision. As of 2026-08-11 no 2026 monthly-update news posts have yet been published this year (only one topical article dated 2026-06-03), so all listed occurrences are projected from the historical pattern.

reports.title: Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries
reports.description: NATO's annual compilation of Allied defence spending against an agreed NATO definition of defence expenditure, distinct from national budget definitions.

release_schedule.note: NATO has no published release calendar or stated rule for this report; it publishes an annual updated compendium of member defence-spending tables/PDF/Excel each year, timed loosely around early summer (often near the NATO summit), though the exact month has varied: 2014-2021 edition issued 11 Jun 2021, 2014-2022 edition issued 27 Jun 2022, 2014-2023 edition issued ~Jun 2023 with a revised edition on 14 Mar 2024, 2014-2024 edition issued 17 Jun 2024, 2014-2025 edition issued 28 Aug 2025 (data cut-off 3 Jun 2025), and the 2014-2026 edition issued 7 Jul 2026. Given this Jun-Aug spread, the next (2014-2027) edition is projected for roughly June-August 2027; no exact date can be cited.

reports.title: National accounts (ESA 2010)
reports.description: Norwegian national accounts, compiled under an EEA Agreement obligation to implement ESA 2010 despite Norway not being an EU member.

entries.covers: Q2 2026 national accounts (with monthly national accounts data)

release_schedule.note: SSB states quarterly national accounts are normally published in Feb (Q4/prior year), May (Q1), Aug (Q2), and Nov (Q3), i.e. 4 releases per year, matching the corpus's releases_per_year=4. Monthly national accounts updates are currently postponed; monthly series are being published together with the quarterly releases instead.

reports.title: Annual national accounts (2020 Base)
reports.description: French annual national accounts, ESMS-style presentation page describing compliance with ESA 2010 and the transmission programme.

entries.covers: Comptes nationaux annuels en 2026 (2020 base) - projected next release

release_schedule.note: INSEE's own provisional dissemination calendar for national accounts states that 'Comptes de la Nation' (annual national accounts, definitive/semi-definitive/provisional vintages) are released in May each year. Actual publication dates for the last three editions (all under the 2020 base) were 2024-05-31, 2025-05-28, and 2026-05-29, confirming a consistent late-May annual release. Next edition (covering 2026 data) is projected for May 2027; exact day not yet published.

reports.title: Documentation sur la méthodologie — Comptes nationaux annuels (Base 2020)
reports.description: INSEE's detailed Base 2020 methodological fiche library for French annual national accounts — the source-level companion to the ESMS presentation page.

release_schedule.note: This is a methodology reference documentation set (24 individual sheets/documents) for the Base 2020 annual national accounts, not a periodic release with its own calendar. Individual sheets have been updated on scattered dates since the Base 2020 launch (May 30, 2024 for most core documents, with further sheet updates through July 18, 2024 and March 12, 2026), indicating ad hoc revisions rather than a fixed annual publication date. The underlying 'Comptes nationaux annuels' data series itself is annual, but no stated rule or calendar governs when this documentation specifically is next revised.

reports.title: Élaboration des statistiques annuelles d'entreprises (Esane)
reports.description: Annual structural business statistics system combining tax/social administrative data and sectoral enterprise surveys; named as the primary source for non-financial enterprise accounts in Base 2020.

entries.covers: Esane 2021 results (Caractéristiques comptables, financières et d'emploi des entreprises en 2021)
Esane 2022 results (Caractéristiques comptables, financières et d'emploi des entreprises en 2022)
Esane 2023 results (Caractéristiques comptables, financières et d'emploi des entreprises en 2023)
Esane 2024 results (expected next release, not yet published as of 2026-08-11)

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or stated rule was found for Esane on INSEE's site; the 'Politique de diffusion' and 'Fréquence de diffusion' metadata pages only state the frequency is 'Annuelle' without giving specific dates. However, the actual Insee Résultats output series for Esane shows a consistent pattern: results for reference year N are published in September of year N+2 (e.g. 2021 data on 2023-09-25, 2022 data on 2024-09-24, 2023 data on 2025-09-18). As of 2026-08-11, the 2024 results had not yet appeared, so the next release is projected for September 2026 based on this pattern.

reports.title: Manual on measuring Research and Development in ESA 2010
reports.description: Eurostat's 2014 manual implementing R&D as capital formation under ESA 2010, cited by INSEE as the basis for its own R&D capitalisation methodology.
reports.cadence_note: Published 2014, no stated revision schedule. Modelled at the same nominal rate as sna-2008 and other versioned methodological standards in this corpus (roughly once a generation) rather than as a one-off, since it functions as an ongoing methodological reference cited by name, not a single-use document.

release_schedule.note: This is a one-off methodological manual (KS-GQ-14-004), published 2014-08-01, approved by the Eurostat Group of Directors of Macroeconomic Statistics in December 2013, guiding Member States on recognizing R&D as capital formation under ESA 2010. The publisher's own product page shows no revision schedule, no release calendar, and no stated update rule. There is no evidence of periodic re-issuance; it functions as a static reference tied to the ESA 2010 standard rather than a recurring publication.

reports.title: Frascati Manual — Guidelines for Collecting and Reporting Data on Research and Experimental Development
reports.description: OECD's standard for R&D statistics collection, cited by the EU's own R&D manual and, through it, by INSEE as the basis for French R&D expenditure statistics used in national accounts.

release_schedule.note: The Frascati Manual is a methodological guidelines document, not a periodic statistical release. Past editions were published in 1963, 1970, 1976, 1980, 1993, 2002, and 2015 (7th, current edition) — gaps between editions have ranged from 4 to 13 years, with no fixed cadence. OECD's own 'Continuing development of the OECD Frascati Manual' page and a 2024 NESTI document (DSTI/STP/NESTI(2024)3/REV2) explicitly state that NESTI 'does not envisage undertaking a wholesale revision of the Frascati Manual' at this time; instead it is producing supplementary 'complementary guidance' as an OECD Technical Paper annexed to the still-current 2015 edition. There is no calendar, no stated rule, and no consistent periodicity — the releases_per_year value of 0.2 (implying a 5-year cycle) does not match the actual historical pattern (roughly one edition every 8-13 years on average since 2002), and given the explicit 'no revision planned' statement, no fixed number is really appropriate here.

"The data is gathered from the Nordic Statistical Institutes (NSIs), the Nordic Health and Welfare Statistics database maintained by the Nomesco-Nososco committees, other Nordic statistics producers as well as international sources such as Eurostat, OECD." Institutions named, no titled publications.

AGENCY_ONLY, and the finding that generalised the branch's central asymmetry outside statistics entirely. "NATO collects defence expenditure data from Allies and publishes it on a regular basis. Each Ally's Ministry of Defence reports current and estimated future defence expenditure according to an agreed definition." NATO's own definition text (fiscal-year armed-forces payments, pensions, stockpiles, R&D, exclusions for war damage and civil defence) is extensive and precise; the reporting party is always an institution, never a titled national publication.

The amounts represent payments by a national government that have been or will be made during the course of the fiscal year to meet the needs of its armed forces, those of Allies or of the Alliance."

Borderline and explicitly hedged by the original researcher: OECD ICIO names INEGI by institution and table-year ("provided by Mexico's Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI for 2003, 2008 and 2012 tables)") but the researcher's own non_finding on the same material called it "limited to a construction detail, not the general obligation language." Not minted: out of the EU/Europe scope this branch is tracking, and the researcher's own hedge means it should not be treated as a clean counter-example without independent verification.
